title: AnnotationBustR Tutorial
text: main function AnnotationBustR AnnotationBust. function extracts sub-sequence(s) interest accessions writes FASTA files current working directory. addition writing sub-sequences FASTA files, AnnotationBust also generates accession table found sub-sequences written FASTA files can written csv file using base R write.csv. AnnotationBustR requires least two arguments, vector accessions Accessions data frame search terms formatted discussed 3.2 3.3 Terms. Additional arguments include ability specify duplicate genes wish recover vector gene names using Duplicates argument specifying number duplicate instances extract using numeric vector (must length Duplicates) using DuplicateInstances argument. AnnotationBustR also arguments translate coding sequences corresponding peptide sequence setting TranslateSeqs argument TRUE. TranslateSeqs=TRUE, users also specify GenBank translation code number corresponding sequences using TranslateCode argument. list GenBank translaton codes taxa available : https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/Taxonomy/Utils/wprintgc.cgi additional argument AnnotationBust DuplicateSpecies set DuplicateSpecies=TRUE adds accession number species name FASTA file. can useful later analyses involving FASTA files duplicate names FASTA headers can pose problems programs. important note users select DuplicateSpecies=TRUE FASTA file contain species names respected accession number, corresponding accession table either single row per species containing accession numbers subsequence locus found species seperated comma seperate row accession number dependent user chooses TidyAccessions argument (see description ). argument Prefixcan either NULL character vector length 1. Prefix NULL add prefix specified FASTA files. left Prefix=NULL files names just name locus. final argument TidyAccessions effects format final accession table. TidyAccessions=TRUE, sequence single species collapsed single cell per locus accessions seperated commas. TidyAccessions=FALSE leave accession number row accession table. tutorial, use accessions created examples 3.1 object .longest.accessions. vector contains three accessions mitogenomes three species Barbonymus. accessions provide good highlight utility package.look annotations three accessions(https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/nuccore/AP011317.1,https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/nuccore/AP011181.1,https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/nuccore/AB238966.1), can see AP011317 AP011181 annotated similar nomenclature, AB238966 differs substantially (e.x. COI vs CO2, Cyt b vs Cb, etc.). example, use arguments AnnotationBust extract 38 subsequences four accessions (22 tRNAs, 13 CDS, 2 rRNAs, 1 D-loop). specify duplicates, case tRNA-Leu tRNA-Ser, occur twice vertebrate mitogenomes. translate CDS using TranslateSeqs = "" return DNA peptide sequence. single accession species, specify DuplicateSpecies=FALSE FASTA files output prefix “Demo” specifying Prefix="Demo" TiddyAccessions=TRUE. create 38 FASTA files mitochondrial loci mitochondrial genome working director prefix “Demo”. can also use AnnotationBustR extract introns sequences. One limitation introns must annotated within subsequence, lacking accessions (e.x. chloroplasts introns annotated). stated , requires use fourth column search terms, labelled IntronExonNumber, used find number intron extracted. instance, lets imagine want extract coding sequence matK exon 2 intron 1 trnK chloroplast genomes KX687911.1 KX687910.1 set search terms follows using current cpDNAterms:
code: #run AnnotationBust function for two duplicate tRNA genes occuring twice and translate CDS my.seqs <- AnnotationBust(Accessions=my.longest.seqs$Accession, Terms=mtDNAterms,Duplicates=c("tRNA_Leu","tRNA_Ser"), DuplicateInstances=c(2,2), TranslateSeqs="Both", DuplicateSpecies=TRUE, Prefix="Demo", TidyAccessions=TRUE)  #We can return the accession table and write it to a CSV file. my.seqs#retutn the accession table write.csv(my.seqs, file="AccessionTable.csv")#Write the accession table to a csv file #Subset out matK from cpDNAterms cds.terms <- subset(cpDNAterms,cpDNAterms$Feature=="matK") #Create a vecotr of NA so we can merge with the search terms for introns and exons cds.terms <- cbind(cds.terms,(rep(NA,length(cds.terms$Feature)))) colnames(cds.terms)[4] <- "IntronExonNumber"  #Prepare a search term table for the intron and exons to remove #We can start with the cpDNAterms for trnK IntronExon.terms <- subset(cpDNAterms,cpDNAterms$Feature=="trnK") #As we want to go for two exons, we will want the synonyms repeated as we are doing and intron and an exon IntronExon.terms <- rbind(IntronExon.terms,IntronExon.terms)#duplicate the terms IntronExon.terms$Type <- rep(c("intron","intron","exon","exon"))#rep the sequence type we want to extract IntronExon.terms$Feature <- rep(c("trnK_Intron","trnK_Exon2"),each=2) IntronExon.terms <- cbind(IntronExon.terms,rep(c(1,1,2,2)))#Add intron/exon number info colnames(IntronExon.terms)[4] <- "IntronExonNumber"#change column name for number info for IntronExon name  #We can then merge everything together with MergeSearchTerms terms IntronExonExampleTerms <- MergeSearchTerms(IntronExon.terms,cds.terms)  #Run AnnotationBust IntronExon.example <- AnnotationBust(Accessions=c("KX687911.1", "KX687910.1"), Terms=IntronExonExampleTerms, Prefix="DemoIntronExon")
